title: Meta-analysis: respiratory tolerance to regular beta2-agonist use in patients with asthma
authors: Salpeter SR, Ormiston TM, Salpeter EE
population: 22 randomised placebo-controlled trials of at least 1 week of regular short- or long-acting beta2-agonist in asthma, without as-needed beta2-agonist in the placebo group; searches 1966 to June 2003
funder: not stated; the article lists 'Disclosures: None disclosed' and no grant support.
result: Against placebo, regular beta2-agonist use did not change mean FEV1 after treatment or the net FEV1 treatment effect, but reduced the peak FEV1 response to subsequent beta2-agonist by 17.8% (95% CI 8.5% to 27.2%), the FEV1 dose response by 34.8% (24% to 45.7%), the PC20 to bronchoconstrictor stimuli by 26% (11% to 37%), leukocyte beta2-receptor density by 18.3% (5.1% to 31.6%), binding affinity by 23.1% (6.8% to 39.4%) and the in vitro response to isoproterenol by 32.7% (9.0% to 56.5%).
